reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the first three premises for the NiFeCoCrPdx system, but provides no evidence that the same mechanism governs magnetocaloric response and hysteresis in the chemically distinct FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys, which is a critical unsupported leap.
premises: Heat treatment and Pd additions reduce the distribution of exchange energies in NiFeCoCrPdx alloys.
Reducing the distribution of exchange energies leads to a more magnetically homogeneous alloy.
A more magnetically homogeneous alloy enhances refrigerant capacity (magnetocaloric response).
These mechanisms and effects observed in NiFeCoCrPdx will generalize to non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloys.
